tickets.title: Fix public contracts and choose compatible native dependencies
tickets.scope: Publish a small interface revision for model, sets, programs, families, evidence and execution. Choose matrix, LP, convex, parser, test and build integrations before adapter work starts.
acceptance: Record supported properties, ownership, error outcomes and performance costs at each interface. No solver-library container appears in a public problem/result type.
Record candidate versions, license constraints, supported toolchains and an integration probe for each selected dependency. Do not change the undecided project license.
Provide caller examples for the two synthesis strategies and independent workspaces. Keep numerical evidence separate from validated claims.

tickets.title: Build and run a portable C++20 client with test support
tickets.scope: Deliver a native client and test entry point that builds selected modules without backend-private headers.
acceptance: Provide repeatable configure, build, test and install commands; record initial platform support and dependency versions.
Run a small backend-neutral client and a literal numeric fixture in CI. Keep generated builds and vendored sources outside tracked scientific artifacts.
Document unavailable sanitizers/platform counters rather than treating a missing tool as a passed check.

tickets.title: Provide owning numeric data and safe matrix views
tickets.scope: Allow clients and adapters to share immutable numeric data without exposing an external matrix type.
acceptance: Check dense/sparse shape, stride, scalar and owner lifetime at input seams; define zero-sized data behavior.
For matrix [[1,2,3],[4,5,6]] and vector [7,11,13], all supported layouts yield [68,161].
Retained asynchronous views preserve ownership; workers do not mutate shared input values.

tickets.title: Select compatible algorithm adapters through a registry
tickets.scope: Resolve registered methods, set operations and backend workspaces from capabilities and requested evidence.
acceptance: Register at least two distinct compatible adapters without editing model or client dispatch logic.
Reject unsupported representation/objective/scalar/guarantee requests before allocation-heavy work; include a reason and actual method identity.
Create independent mutable workspaces from immutable configuration; no portable cross-compiler C++ ABI is claimed.

tickets.title: Define affine LTI/LTV models and separate observations
tickets.scope: Construct reusable immutable dynamics and observation models with explicit time and input roles.
acceptance: Represent A/B/E/offset and observation/error/feedthrough maps, including singular A and absent ports.
Compact LTI and explicit LTV providers agree for x0=2, A=3, B=2, a=-1, u=[1,-2]: states [2,7,16].
Validate timestamps and pre/post-action availability. No observations does not grant full-state knowledge.

tickets.title: Represent control domains, constraints and initial information
tickets.scope: Build problems with explicit stagewise constraints and natural general-model special cases.
acceptance: Keep point/set initial information, continuous/finite/mixed domains and external-input semantics distinct; first nominal profile uses a known point.
Distinguish universal, empty, singleton and bounded sets. T transitions use T control and T+1 state stages.
Retain optional temporal constraints and future hybrid identity without silently relaxing discrete choices or erasing uncertainty quantifiers.

tickets.title: Validate complete problems and strategy assumptions
tickets.scope: Validate mathematical inputs separately from configured strategy support.
acceptance: Report shape/index/criterion errors separately from unsupported, infeasible and solver failure.
Keep singular/unbounded/lower-dimensional problems representable while an inverse/compact-set strategy declares its restrictions.
Bind resolved problem identity to mathematical data and external content, independent of selected backend settings.

tickets.title: Represent exact polyhedral and elementary sets
tickets.scope: Provide immutable H/V set data and empty/singleton/universal cases with explicit evidence.
acceptance: Retain ambient and affine dimension, equality rows, vertices/rays where applicable, coordinate labels and representation ID.
Keep algebraic equivalence distinct from numerical/validated evidence. Lower-dimensional sets are not rejected by the data model.
Clients can query metadata without copying or materializing payloads.

tickets.title: Evaluate and reformulate structured terminal objectives
tickets.scope: Support linear, convex quadratic and affine residual-norm criteria with independent original-cost evaluation.
acceptance: Validate coefficient shapes, symmetry/PSD evidence policy and rectangular residual maps.
Record norm-square reformulation Q=2L^TL, q=-2L^Tr, c=r^Tr; report the original norm after solving.
Cover zero residual and semidefinite/constant criteria without assuming a unique terminal minimizer.

tickets.title: Expose linear-program and basis-diagnostic interfaces
tickets.scope: Give hull, geometry and recovery algorithms a backend-neutral LP interface.
acceptance: Describe equality/inequality rows, variable bounds and objective conventions without a backend container.
Separate termination, infeasible/unbounded outcomes, primal/dual residuals and justified bounds.
Make basis/pivot data optional capabilities; use one exclusive workspace per worker.

tickets.title: Integrate a reference native LP adapter
tickets.scope: Run geometry and recovery LPs through the native dependency selected by CORE-01.
acceptance: Register the adapter and translate real statuses and residuals. Feasibility/finite optimum/infeasible/unbounded analytic fixtures pass.
Reuse compatible native workspaces without sharing mutable solver state between workers.
Retain raw diagnostics and version identity; do not fabricate certificates unavailable from the backend.

tickets.title: Implement the archival phase-I feasibility kernel
tickets.scope: Implement the professor-associated phase-I procedure for the equality/nonnegative feasibility tasks used by hull and recovery modules.
acceptance: Document lineage from L01/L03/L07 and A06; do not claim one saved variant is a verified original release.
Return feasible coefficients, auxiliary residual, basis/pivot diagnostics and bounded termination. Define degeneracy and anti-cycling policy.
Check triangle membership, collinear inputs, signed coordinates and deterministic pivot ties against the reference LP.

tickets.title: Reduce hulls with independent membership LPs
tickets.scope: Deliver a baseline HullReducer that retains the same convex hull and original point identity.
acceptance: Remove p only with supported nonnegative convex-combination evidence relative to other retained points.
Handle empty/singleton, duplicates, face points and lower-dimensional clouds; record LP calls and outcomes.
Verify hull equality independently by support/membership queries instead of comparing vertex order.

tickets.title: Add basis-reuse hull classification as a replaceable method
tickets.scope: Use completed phase-I basis information to classify multiple hull candidates without changing the HullReducer interface.
acceptance: Distinguish within-solve bulk classification from cross-query warm starts; preserve input point IDs.
Validate every bulk removal; skipped basis points need a proof or final verification pass.
Compare permuted, degenerate and interior-basis clouds with the baseline hull. Publish LP/pivot/bulk counters without a universal speedup claim.

tickets.title: Add ordered and grouped hull reduction strategies
tickets.scope: Expose the archive ordering/grouping methods inspired by divide-and-conquer as distinct HullReducer adapters.
acceptance: Identify which Scientific Research and Constrained QLPHULL steps actually run; document commented-out sections and differences.
Sorting, filtering, grouping and final reduction preserve hull equality for every input permutation and degeneracy fixture.
Declare this as a hull-level strategy, separate from LP pivot rules and recursive QuickHull; expose grouping/order counters.

tickets.title: Integrate convex-program interfaces and a reference adapter
tickets.scope: Solve supported terminal convex programs through a registered QP/conic adapter.
acceptance: Declare supported objective, equalities, lower-dimensional sets and evidence scope before execution.
Check inside/boundary optima, zero residual and semidefinite minima against analytic answers.
Return point and optimality evidence without claiming it already describes every terminal minimizer.

tickets.title: Implement the Pascal-derived Zoutendijk projection method
tickets.scope: Add a feasible-direction adapter for Euclidean projection onto a supported linearly constrained set, using A06 ZODENTEK as source evidence.
acceptance: Record the active-constraint direction LP and feasible-start policy. Implement the smooth quadratic equivalent and retain original projection distance.
The step bound checks all positive directional derivatives; regression has an inactive zero-derivative row before a later finite bound.
Compare interval/box/face/singleton projections with analytic and reference QP results; feasible iterates, zero direction, termination and KKT residual are explicit.

tickets.title: Extend feasible directions to declared smooth convex objectives
tickets.scope: Add a reviewed differentiable-convex feasible-direction adapter without treating generic callbacks as certified convex programs.
acceptance: Specify objective/gradient and linear-constraint contracts, line-search conditions and supported convergence/optimality evidence.
Handle zero direction, infeasible starts and numerical stalls distinctly; compare analytic smooth convex cases with a trusted solver.
Document ALOWER/projected-gradient source differences; nonconvex or unsupported constraints do not acquire global-optimum labels.

tickets.title: Compute polyhedral affine images and Minkowski sums
tickets.scope: Provide exact mathematical affine/sum operations used by forward propagation.
acceptance: Check support identities on analytic intervals/squares, singular maps and rectangular control maps.
Preserve empty/singleton and coordinate/evidence metadata; reduce generated candidates through the chosen HullReducer.
Finite action sets are not silently replaced by their convex hull.

tickets.title: Convert H and V descriptions with equality and ray support
tickets.scope: Register a reviewed H/V conversion adapter that handles the declared set class.
acceptance: Round-trip square, simplex, embedded segment and singleton by independent membership/support checks.
Translate empty/unbounded/equality/ray outcomes honestly; a bounded-only adapter rejects unsupported requests.
Record conversion identity, time, input/output sizes and numeric evidence; audit A17/A18 lineage without assuming executable equivalence.

tickets.title: Intersect state sets and remove redundant inequalities
tickets.scope: Apply state constraints without losing newly created intersection vertices.
acceptance: Test crossing edges with all original vertices outside the constraint, empty intersections and affine equality rows.
Remove a halfspace only after an implication LP establishes supported nonpositive maximum violation.
Preserve essential bounding rows, equality conventions and T+1 state indexing.

tickets.title: Project joint polyhedra and compute nominal predecessors
tickets.scope: Compute existential preimages/projections with explicit coordinate maps and no global invertibility restriction.
acceptance: Implement {x in X: exists u in U, Ax+Bu+a in S}; test singular A, unreachable target and analytic integrator cases.
An inverse-based fast adapter may require nonsingular A, but a general projection route remains a separate capability.
Projection can remain lazy until a supported query requests materialization; preserve equality/ray and evidence semantics.

tickets.title: Add a separate two-dimensional QuickHull adapter
tickets.scope: Provide a geometric 2D hull alternative for exact projected clouds and method comparison.
acceptance: Audit Scientific Research quickhull and use a documented independent implementation, not an LP-kernel alias.
Handle duplicates, collinear/all-coincident data and orientation ties; retain original point identities.
Compare hull equality with the LP reference. Reject higher dimensions instead of projecting silently.

tickets.title: Add zonotope and constrained-zonotope exact operations
tickets.scope: Register generator-based representations and their supported exact operations with dependency-preserving factors.
acceptance: Affine images and sums preserve shared factor identities; constrained-generator equalities are not erased.
Document closure restrictions and explicit equivalent conversions; unsupported intersections do not become ordinary zonotopes by silent approximation.
Use boxes, line segments and constrained-factor examples checked by polyhedral reference queries.

tickets.title: Provide lazy support queries and controlled materialization
tickets.scope: Let set callers query support and affine/projection expressions without mandatory full vertex enumeration.
acceptance: Record expression operands, arithmetic/evidence and immutable ownership; support answers match analytic and polyhedral references.
Materialization is an explicit budgeted operation with cancellation and representation-growth reporting.
Finite direction samples are labelled as samples/enclosures under their stated construction, not a complete exact set.

tickets.title: Define inner and outer approximation policies and evidence
tickets.scope: Expose approximation as a separate registered operation with a reference set, direction and budget.
acceptance: Equivalent conversion, inner, outer and heuristic output use distinct labels and capability checks.
For R_in subset R subset R_out, supported objective bounds retain direction; an inner reachable state needs a realizable trajectory for an achievable plan.
Reject a requested enclosure guarantee when inclusion evidence is unavailable; reachable-set approximation does not imply the same relation for optimizer families.

tickets.title: Implement box and parallelotope approximations
tickets.scope: Add simple-set enclosure adapters under declared assumptions.
acceptance: Check outer support-direction bounds on intervals/rotated polygons; chosen inner constructions verify every contained vertex or another valid certificate.
Record orientation, budget, approximation error when justified and input/output representation sizes.
Degenerate, empty and unbounded inputs receive supported output or a clear capability result.

tickets.title: Implement zonotope reduction and enclosure adapters
tickets.scope: Control generator growth with explicit enclosure direction and selectable algorithms.
acceptance: Exact removal and conservative reduction are distinct; verify analytic inclusion/support bounds on fixed examples.
Preserve shared-factor dependencies or record their explicit relaxation. Intersections advertise their actual resulting class.
Record generator budget, realized size and objective/witness limitations; compare with A04 and owner zonotope paper after source ambiguities are resolved.

tickets.title: Implement ellipsoidal approximation and reference comparison
tickets.scope: Add directional ellipsoidal enclosures and an optional external Ellipsoidal Toolbox comparison adapter.
acceptance: Declare supported input class and formulas; check shape PSD, degenerate sets and actual inclusion direction.
Keep finite ellipsoidal families and their intersection/union semantics explicit; do not assume closure by one ellipsoid.
Pin external ET inputs/version if used; no missing MATLAB dependency is presented as a completed native verification.

tickets.title: Propagate nominal reachable sets with stage constraints
tickets.scope: Compute the nominal tube for selected exact set operations and preserve recovery information.
acceptance: Apply (A_t R_t plus B_t U_t plus a_t) intersect X_(t+1) with correct stage order and initial constraints.
Check analytic integrators and an LTV sequence independently; cancellation and empty reachable stages have explicit outcomes.
Keep selected method/representation and shared factors visible; per-stage marginals are not reported as the complete optimal family.

tickets.title: Construct the entire terminal minimizer relation
tickets.scope: Return supported full terminal argmin sets and optimum evidence, including nonunique convex minima.
acceptance: Linear optimal faces, constant objectives and semidefinite/residual-map degeneracy preserve all terminal optima.
Document and independently check the convex quadratic/residual optimal-level characterization used to build the relation; one solver point alone is insufficient.
Attainment, finite optimum and numerical completeness limits are explicit; unsupported nonpolyhedral argmin construction is rejected.

tickets.title: Build optimal families by reachability and backward recovery
tickets.scope: Implement the historical-method-based strategy with complete joint-history semantics.
acceptance: Recover the feasible preimage of the entire terminal minimizer relation, retaining cross-stage state/control dependence.
For the two-step integrator, represent u0+u1=1 and reject (1,1); for a constant criterion preserve every feasible trajectory.
Separate extensions for family completeness from the archived single-witness algorithm; record assumptions and any inverse-only fast-path limits.

tickets.title: Build optimal families by direct joint-trajectory optimization
tickets.scope: Solve the sparse full-trajectory program and construct its optimal relation behind the common synthesis interface.
acceptance: Encode every transition, initial/stage constraint and original terminal objective; no hidden state-constraint omission.
Return supported complete families as relations, not a single QP minimizer; do not use Cartesian control marginals.
Check the same analytic cases as the reachability strategy, including singular A and multiple histories for one terminal point.

tickets.title: Extract different complete witnesses without changing optimality
tickets.scope: Select controls and their consistent trajectories from either family through one query interface.
acceptance: Record selection directions/seed and requested/returned/distinct counts; duplicates use explicit tolerance.
Extract (0,1) and (1,0) for the analytic integrator and keep primary cost zero; singleton results are distinguished from failure to find more.
Query termination and memory are independent of solve termination; no uniform random or uniqueness guarantee is invented.

tickets.title: Verify trajectories and evidence independently
tickets.scope: Recompute original problem residuals and verify evidence bindings without trusting the synthesis result flag.
acceptance: Detect injected wrong transition, bound violation and objective mismatch with named residuals/tolerances.
Keep feasibility, optimality, family completeness and validated claims separate; reject evidence for a different problem identity.
Retain backend bound provenance and unsupported-verification results without certifying family completeness from sampled witnesses.

tickets.title: Load and validate versioned scenario files
tickets.scope: Accept short user-authored scenarios and optional run settings without C++ edits.
acceptance: Freeze syntax/schema through CORE-01, infer and cross-check dimensions, and document stable resolved defaults.
Malformed shape/stage/schema and unknown fields identify the field and expected form; no guessed bounds or automatic discretization.
Backend changes preserve mathematical scenario identity; historical non-executable records retain restoration diagnostics.

tickets.title: Select scenarios and run method profiles from a native CLI
tickets.scope: Provide a simple launcher for choosing a scenario, validating it and running the two selected methods.
acceptance: Basic use selects a file and default comparison profile; backend/seed/resources remain optional overrides.
Return actionable capability/input failures and save final versioned results through the artifact interface.
CLI contains no duplicated optimization logic and supports validation-only execution without an expensive solve.

tickets.title: Publish simple executable templates with known answers
tickets.scope: Give users a small selectable template catalogue and instructions for their own files.
acceptance: Provide minimal LTI, state-constrained and LTV cases with linear/quadratic/residual-norm examples.
Every executable template has complete data and an independent expected answer; editing requires no build step.
Keep B04-historical separate and non-executable until canonical restoration; state stages, coordinates/units and criterion weights are explained.

tickets.title: Execute isolated workspaces with budgets and cancellation
tickets.scope: Share immutable inputs while controlling mutable solver resources and partial results.
acceptance: Give each worker exclusive workspace/warm-start ownership and a shared outer/BLAS/backend thread budget.
Cancellation/deadline and documented allocation limits preserve available incumbents and evidence; noninterruptible-call latency is recorded.
Parallel and sequential analytic runs agree within stated tolerance; unsupported enforcement is not claimed as a hard limit.

tickets.title: Run independent scenario sweeps within one resource budget
tickets.scope: Scale independent scenarios/seeds/configurations with bounded output and reproducible provenance.
acceptance: Do not treat constrained horizon stages as independent jobs; prioritize coarse runs and compatible set queries.
Avoid nested oversubscription and copy-heavy immutable payload transfer; record actual workers/backend threads and memory support.
Sequential/parallel results retain scenario/configuration IDs, failures and deterministic selection settings.

tickets.title: Add fixed-plan disturbance reachability and global worst-case reference
tickets.scope: Support declared independent bounded process disturbances and a justified worst-case objective oracle.
acceptance: For fixed controls propagate the entire disturbance set; reject robust state violations without clipping away counterexamples.
For supported compact polytopes and convex objectives, evaluate terminal vertices or use another reviewed global bound; a local minimizer of negative convex cost is not a global oracle.
Check interval endpoint maxima, all-infeasible plans and archived B08 rounded-data reference without claiming nonlinear reproduction.

tickets.title: Preserve all optimal branches for finite and mixed control domains
tickets.scope: Provide separate finite/minimax and compatible mixed-domain strategies with complete tie/branch semantics.
acceptance: Stream finite prefixes or use a selected mixed-integer adapter under explicit capabilities.
Retain equal-cost branches and continuous families within them; pruning and DAG merges preserve action identity and history.
Exhaustive tiny examples independently check all ties; convex-hull relaxation of discrete actions is labelled explicitly.

For finite minimax, minimize over fixed control plans the maximum over all admissible disturbance sequences using EXT-01; never replace the global worst case with local minimization of a negated convex cost.

tickets.title: Add temporal-constraint strategies and exact memory lifts
tickets.scope: Support reviewed linear cross-stage constraints through joint relations and specific memory augmentations.
acceptance: Use #9 temporal-coupling proof and counterexample; define initial memory and original/auxiliary coordinate maps.
Test the counterexample that physical-state-only propagation loses coupling, plus both directions of the one-step slew lift.
New constrained studies have new scenario IDs; first archival inputs remain unchanged and unsupported robust/geometry combinations are rejected.

tickets.title: Add initial-set semantics and observation-based control workflows
tickets.scope: Keep uncertain initial information, estimation and feedback distinct from nominal point-initialized planning.
acceptance: Specify existential versus all-initial-states planning and available observation history; no initial-set union silently becomes one robust plan.
Implement a supported controller/estimator lifecycle with pre/post-decision timing and per-step evidence.
Use separate scenario variants and tests for partial/noisy observations; sampled simulation does not certify every disturbance.

tickets.title: Discretize continuous models through an explicit model adapter
tickets.scope: Allow later continuous-time input with explicit physical times and input-hold/integration semantics.
acceptance: Distinguish continuous coefficients from already-discrete transitions in schema and model metadata.
Check analytic LTI zero-order-hold examples and reviewed LTV integration references; retain integration/error provenance.
Descriptor/singular continuous mass matrices and nonlinear models remain separate capabilities, not one extra optional matrix.

tickets.title: Verify claim-specific certificates with validated arithmetic
tickets.scope: Add a concrete verifier for selected feasibility/inclusion/objective claims rather than a generic proof flag.
acceptance: Choose a certificate class and compatible rounding-aware arithmetic; bind assumptions and problem identity.
Separate supported claim coverage from family completeness and model-error certification; reject unsupported validated requests.
Check exact/rational or interval reference fixtures and adversarial rounding cases; failed or inconclusive certificates are not accepted.

tickets.title: Add a recursive split-and-merge hull strategy
tickets.scope: Implement a new hull-level divide-and-conquer strategy using hull(hull(P1) union hull(P2)). The archive supports ordered/grouped filtering and a separate 2D QuickHull; this recursive LP-backed strategy is a new extension. Reuse the hull port and selected membership backend.
acceptance: Provide the finite-point hull-equivalence argument and deterministic partition/merge policy before code; stop small leaves with the existing reducer.
Compare hull support and removed-point certificates with the independent baseline on signed, duplicate and affine-degenerate fixtures, across input permutations.
Use exclusive child workspaces and a common resource budget; record leaf/merge LP work, peak intermediate point counts and parallel overhead without claiming a universal speedup.

tickets.title: Add optional cross-query LP warm starts
tickets.scope: Add compatible-backend warm starts as an optional workspace optimization. The archival basis-reuse method reuses classifications within one completed solve; it does not establish this new cross-query feature.
acceptance: Define basis validity, problem-change compatibility, invalidation and fallback without exposing backend containers.
Cold and warm paths give the same independently checked membership/status on changed rows, columns, bounds and degenerate cases; incompatible hints fall back or diagnose.
State belongs to one workspace; compare cold/warm setup and solve work with explicit cache state, including a case where reuse costs more.

tickets.title: Implement an independent nonlinear replay adapter
tickets.scope: Implement replay of complete controls on an independently specified plant. Start with an analytic nonlinear toy plant; accept B04 only when its plant parameters and timing conventions are sourced. This is simulation, with no nonlinear optimization claim.
acceptance: Declare plant parameters, initial state, integration method, tolerances and control-hold convention; missing data return named prerequisites.
For x_next=x+u+u^2, x0=0, controls (0,1) and (0.5,0.5) have terminal states 2 and 1.5, although both give 1 under the linear integrator; independently check these values.
Preserve original plant units and objective, numerical diagnostics, plant identity and separate replay timing; no fitted archival coefficients or invented histories.

tickets.title: Expand historical optimizer and hull-variant differential tests
tickets.scope: Expand independent tests for phase-I, within-solve basis classification, grouping, recursive reduction, warm starts and Pascal-derived Zoutendijk projection. Each implementation already ships minimum acceptance tests.
acceptance: Check barycentric certificates and hull support against the trusted LP baseline for degenerate bases, signed/flat clouds, permutations and pivot ties; basis membership alone is not extreme-point evidence.
Check all positive directional constraint derivatives when bounding a Zoutendijk step; include a row with nonpositive derivative before a later finite limiting row.
Projection onto [0,1]^2 of (2,-1) is (1,0), distance sqrt(2); include already-feasible points, zero gradient, infeasible constraints and numerical limits.
Counters include every child LP call; warm-state isolation and fallback tests compare mathematical answers rather than expected speedups.
QuickHull agrees with an independent 2D monotone-chain/orientation oracle on vertical, collinear, repeated, empty-side and rotated fixtures; no slope division assumes nonvertical edges.

tickets.title: Expand exact structured-set and approximation contract tests
tickets.scope: Test the implemented zonotope/constrained-zonotope operations and box, parallelotope, zonotope and ellipsoidal approximations against independent low-dimensional inclusion oracles. Each adapter ships its own minimum tests first.
acceptance: Compare exact supported affine/sum operations against analytic supports; intersection is not assumed closed in ordinary zonotopes.
For a known box/triangle, check claimed inclusion by a valid analytic or complete low-dimensional oracle; sampled directions are labelled samples, not containment proofs.
Test degenerate dimensions, empty input, infeasible recovery, incompatible guarantee requests and unsupported operations; external ET comparison never becomes a runtime requirement.
Outer reachability alone cannot supply realizable optimal controls; inner-set cost bounds require a recovery witness and compatible objective assumptions.

tickets.title: Review optimizer variants, structured sets and approximation scalability
tickets.scope: Perform independent standards and specification reviews of the later optimizer/representation adapters, proof assumptions, module seams and measured output costs.
acceptance: Record reviewed commits, file/line findings, severity and reproducible counterexamples; the implementer cannot self-sign off.
Confirm LP kernels, hull policies, conversion operators and approximations can change independently; test replacement with actual compatible adapters.
Audit hull preservation, active-constraint step bounds, inclusion direction, numerical versus validated evidence and witness realizability.
Inspect allocation/materialization costs, workspace ownership and benchmark equivalence; linked blocking fixes are rechecked before closure.
Include the geometric QuickHull adapter and its independent orientation/degeneracy tests; keep its geometry strategy distinct from the LP-backed recursive reducer.

tickets.title: Expand declared extension profiles with independent quantifier oracles
tickets.scope: Add profile-specific mathematical tests only for the implemented extension demonstrations. Robust fixed plans, information-based policies, mixed controls and discretization retain separate capability suites; this does not certify a universal hybrid solver.
acceptance: Enumerate a tiny finite-action/vertex-disturbance problem independently, preserve all tied optimal branches, and detect a disturbance path that must not be clipped to a state constraint.
Compare the approved slew-memory lift to exhaustive short-history feasibility; distinguish initial-set union versus universal feasibility and observation information available before a decision.
For the constant scalar continuous system x_dot=2x+u with zero-order hold, compare the discretization with exp(2h) and (exp(2h)-1)/2; record integration and hold assumptions.
Tamper with claim-specific certificate/problem IDs and fail verification; unsupported nonlinear/hybrid or evidence profiles diagnose rather than inherit a guarantee.

tickets.title: Review extension quantifiers, information patterns and native scalability
tickets.scope: Review the explicitly implemented future profiles and their scientific assumptions. Separate representability from algorithm support; do not broaden a finite demonstration into general robust, feedback or hybrid completeness.
acceptance: Independently inspect disturbance quantifier order, fixed-plan versus feedback semantics, finite/mixed branch completeness and all tied optima.
Audit temporal-lift equivalence, observation causality, discretization assumptions and certificate scope against referenced proofs and counterexamples.
Check extension registration without fuel-specific core switches, exclusive worker state, bounded materialization and measured complexity.
Record reviewed commits and actionable findings; linked blocking fixes must pass independent re-review.

tickets.title: Expand native buffer, ownership and build-boundary tests
tickets.scope: Test C++20 owning values/views, storage/stride conventions and native module boundaries (RUN-01/02, ALG-07). Limit: memory-safety tooling and compile probes support declared platforms; they do not establish a portable C++ ABI.
acceptance: Use a fixed nonsquare matrix [[1,2,3],[4,5,6]] and vector [7,11,13]: each supported row/column-major or strided view yields [68,161] against a hand-calculated oracle; malformed stride/shape is diagnosed.
Exercise copy/move and retained-owner asynchronous paths; destroy source owners at controlled points and check documented retention or rejection rather than relying on incidental object lifetime.
Compile a backend-neutral public-client fixture without matrix/solver private include paths; verify installed headers contain no selected backend container dependency.
Run supported sanitizer/debug-iterator checks with recorded toolchain; zero-length ports have defined behavior and no invalid access.

The originating implementation ships with meaningful minimum acceptance tests written before its code; this separate issue expands the suite using independently designed oracles and records discovered defects as fixes.

tickets.title: Expand affine model and observation contract tests
tickets.scope: Test compositional immutable LTI/LTV dynamics, zero-dimensional channels and pre/post-decision observation semantics (MOD-01/02/03/04/09). Limit: model representability does not imply initial nominal strategy support.
acceptance: Compare compact constant coefficients with explicit stage providers using fixed independent trajectories; x0=2, A=3, B=2, a=-1, controls [1,-2] must give states [2,7,16].
Reject wrong A/B/E/offset shapes and stage indices; enforce T transitions versus T+1 states and document the selected zero-horizon policy.
Keep absent controls/external channels, zero-valued singleton channels and unrestricted channels semantically distinct; no observation never becomes full-state knowledge.
Test separate observation channels, partial/full observations, offsets and measurement errors; pre-decision dependence on unavailable current control produces a causal diagnostic.
Discrete matrices are used directly even when timestamps are nonunit; continuous-time data are distinguished and rejected by the initial loader/planner.

The originating implementation ships with meaningful minimum acceptance tests written before its code; this separate issue expands the suite using independently designed oracles and records discovered defects as fixes.

tickets.title: Expand problem validation and whole-pipeline capability tests
tickets.scope: Test problem composition, reusable models and early capability diagnostics (MOD-05/06/07/08/09, ALG-04/05). Limit: future disturbance/feedback/finite/hybrid/temporal/arithmetic capabilities are representable or rejected; this suite does not implement them.
acceptance: Reuse one immutable model with two constraints/objectives and compare against distinct hand-derived feasible regions; run settings cannot mutate problem data.
Singular A is accepted by the model; a registered inverse-only strategy returns unsupported with the offending stage while a compatible noninverse path is not rejected merely for singularity.

Finite/mixed domains remain distinguishable from continuous convex hulls; empty temporal constraints pass and unsupported nonempty coupling, uncertain initial quantifier, disturbance or feedback requests get specific diagnostics.

Inject missing downstream operation, incompatible output guarantee, noncompact vertex-only input and validated-evidence requests; a counting backend confirms validation fails before expensive solve/workspace execution.

Empty admissibility means mathematical infeasibility; missing unsupported operator means unsupported; nonfinite or malformed numerical data follow documented validation rather than becoming infeasibility.

The originating implementation ships with meaningful minimum acceptance tests written before its code; this separate issue expands the suite using independently designed oracles and records discovered defects as fixes.

tickets.title: Expand objective evaluation and justified reformulation tests
tickets.scope: Test the linear, convex-quadratic and rectangular residual-norm modules independently of solvers (OPT-01/02). Limit: convexity is checked under the declared numerical policy; a numerical PSD check is not a validated certificate.
acceptance: At x=[1,2], linear c=[2,-1], d=3 gives 3; Q=diag(2,0), q=[0,1], c=3 gives 6 using the one-half convention.
For L=[[1,0,0],[0,1,1]], r=[1,4], x=[1,1,3], the norm is zero; at x=[4,1,7], original norm is 5 and squared solver cost is 25.
Use analytic bounded minimizer sets to show norm/square give the same minimizers while reporting different original versus transformed values; include zero residual and rank-deficient L.
Reject wrong rectangular-map dimensions, materially nonsymmetric/indefinite Q and nonfinite data under documented tolerances.
A sum containing other objective terms cannot inherit the pure norm-to-square equivalence; transformation provenance records weights, offsets and conventions.

The originating implementation ships with meaningful minimum acceptance tests written before its code; this separate issue expands the suite using independently designed oracles and records discovered defects as fixes.

tickets.title: Run reusable LP adapter contracts on every selected backend
tickets.scope: Test LP port, backend status translation and optional simplex diagnostics (ALG-01/02, SOL-03). Limit: tests only claim bounds/rays/certificates actually supported by each adapter; passing examples do not verify arbitrary backend correctness.

tickets.title: Implement nested and parallel timing with explicit wall and CPU semantics
tickets.scope: Goal: supply a lightweight ExecutionContext timing collector for OBS-01. Requirements RUN-02/03/04 and EXP-01/04. Use a monotonic wall clock, optional CPU clock with process/thread scope explicitly stated, and an injectable clock for tests. Keep the disabled collector cheap. Do not enforce platform-specific CPU or peak-memory counters where unavailable, or claim parent/child times are additive.
acceptance: A deterministic fake-clock nested example distinguishes inclusive duration from exclusive wall time computed by child interval union; parent and child inclusive durations are never summed as an end-to-end total.

Overlapping parallel spans report run wall latency separately from sum of worker work durations. CPU metrics declare thread/process scope and availability; shared process CPU deltas are not attributed independently to overlapping children.
Cross-thread task parentage and span IDs survive concurrent collection without sharing mutable solver workspaces, data races, or double-counting the same span.
RAII scope closure records cancelled, failed and resource-limited operations; clock anomalies and incomplete spans are diagnosed rather than producing plausible false totals.
Disabled collection retains results/evidence and yields explicitly absent detailed metrics; test overhead as a benchmark measurement, not a fragile wall-clock unit-test threshold.

acceptance: Expose per-module/operation call counts, total and distribution of inclusive wall/work durations, explicitly defined exclusive metrics when available, CPU scope/availability, input/output representation sizes, solver iterations when supplied, and memory scope/availability.

Report setup/family/first-query/additional-query/verification/end-to-end/plot-export phases with median and a documented tail statistic across measured repetitions; do not sum overlapping inclusive phases into latency.

Place objective in its original convention, residuals, justified gaps, feasibility/optimality/completeness evidence and approximation direction alongside timing so differing outputs cannot appear as identical work.

A deterministic fixture with nested parallel spans yields independently hand-calculated aggregates and exports unavailable, unsupported and failed values explicitly; unit labels and precision prevent misleading zeros.
Raw per-run data, schema version and provenance accompany the table, allowing another tool to recreate it without a live solve; historical reported numbers use a separate provenance-labelled track.

tickets.title: Prepare backend-neutral final control and state plot data
tickets.scope: Goal: define a PlotData adapter that consumes final comparison artifacts and independently verified complete witnesses. Requirements SOL-04/05, EXP-01/06, EVD-01/02. Sources: modular architecture and B04 tables/restoration. Outputs carry state/control coordinates, units, stage/time axes, method/witness identities, known bounds/targets, objective and evidence labels. Rendering is outside synthesis/geometry/optimization; no frontend, Python binding or interactive intermediate viewer is selected here.
acceptance: Controls use T stage intervals and states T+1 stage points; optional physical timestamps are used only when supplied and do not discretize dynamics. The control hold convention is explicit where a physical-time step plot is shown.
Plot every selected witness with stable method/witness identity and common axes; label samples as selected complete witnesses rather than the whole optimal family.
Expose original objective, residual/evidence references, requested/returned/distinct counts and duplicate diagnostics; a path marked invalid or unverified cannot be displayed as certified optimal.

For fuel metadata preserve oxidizer flow/working-stock balance and fuel flow/working-stock balance, units kg/s and kg, and source targets/flow bounds. Negative stock balance remains visible without an invented nonnegative constraint.

An analytic two-step fixture validates axis indexing and control/state alignment; malformed witness lengths, evidence/problem mismatch and missing physical-time conventions give explicit errors or stage-only plots.

tickets.title: Support selectable fuel-state 2D plots with explicit projection guarantees
tickets.scope: Goal: add a final PlotRequest accepting coordinate pairs, with trajectory-pair views available immediately and mathematical set projections only on explicit request. Requirements EXP-01/06, ALG-03/04/05 and reserved SOL-06 projection capability, refined by the owner's fuel 2D projection request. Sources: set-representation review and B04 restoration. Inputs name state/control relation, stage when applicable, coordinate pair and required guarantee; outputs bind projected data to the same problem, stage and set/family identity. Exclude all-stage intermediate reachable-set viewers and automatic full-dimensional vertex materialization.
acceptance: The four-state fuel case accepts any distinct in-range state pair, including flow/flow, stock/stock and flow/stock, with correct labels/units; repeated/out-of-range coordinates reject clearly.

Without an explicit set-projection query, render only selected trajectory coordinate pairs and terminal samples. Spy operators prove ordinary trajectory export invokes no exact projection or H/V conversion.

An explicit final reachable-set or optimal-family projection request calls a compatible registered operator, records query cost and reference identity, and returns unsupported if its required exact/equivalent guarantee cannot be met.

Distinguish exact projected geometry under declared arithmetic evidence, inner/outer enclosures, heuristic shapes and finite witness/support samples in plot data and legends; an outer approximation or sampled convex hull is never relabelled exact.

Use a hand-derived rectangle and lower-dimensional line projection oracle; test empty/unbounded/unsupported cases according to implemented capabilities, and retain cross-stage dependence claims separately from displayed 2D marginals.
test_ids: T-VIZ02: analytic 2D projection and no-query spy oracle

tickets.title: Export standalone scientific final-result figures
tickets.scope: Goal: render PlotData and performance-table records with standard scientific plotting tools into standalone vector figures and raster previews. Requirements EXP-01/02/04/06. Choose and document a plotting/export adapter after dependency review; a standalone external plotting tool is allowed and does not select public language bindings. Inputs are saved artifacts and PlotRequest; outputs include control/state figures, selected 2D pair figures and detailed timing charts/tables. Plotting/export stays outside solver logic, and interactive intermediate viewing is optional future scope.
acceptance: Export standalone SVG or PDF plus PNG with axes, units, readable legends, method/witness labels, objective/evidence context, approximation/sample labels and scenario identity. Figures open and remain interpretable without an app or live solver.
Support plot regeneration from saved raw data with a versioned style/export configuration; record plotting-tool version and export timing separately from mathematical solve/query latency.

Provide fuel flow/stock state plots, stage-aligned controls and requested 2D coordinate pairs; visually inspect exported artifacts for clipped labels, indistinguishable series, hidden negative balances and misleading projection legends.
A timing figure preserves wall-versus-work/CPU definitions and labels unavailable metrics; it does not show overlapping inclusive durations as an additive latency stack.
Integration tests validate artifact contents and numerical series against an analytic fixture, while documented visual QA checks the produced figures; avoid brittle exact-pixel assertions.
test_ids: T-VIZ03: regenerated standalone figure integration and visual QA

tickets.title: Associate nonlinear replay results with linearly optimal witnesses
tickets.scope: Goal: extend final comparison/plot artifacts with optional independent plant replay records for complete selected linear witnesses. Requirements EXP-01/02/04, EVD-01/02 and SOL-04/05. Sources: b04-tables.md and b04-restoration.md. Inputs are witness history, explicit reference-plant identity/parameters/initial conditions and integration/control-hold conventions; outputs store replay trajectory, original replay objective, numerical/integration diagnostics and distinct replay timing. This ticket consumes a separately implemented plant adapter. It neither implements nonlinear optimization nor chooses the best replay witness as a new primary objective.
acceptance: A linear witness links to separate linear verification and nonlinear replay records; labels distinguish linear optimality evidence, nonlinear feasibility/quality and absence of nonlinear global-optimality evidence.

Different linearly optimal witnesses can produce distinct replay trajectories/costs without being called inconsistent linear solver results; original objective convention and plant units are preserved.

Missing plant parameters, initial conditions, full controls or integration/hold conventions yield unavailable replay with named prerequisites; no interpolation of historical controls or fitted coefficients fills gaps silently.

Keep nominal reference, frozen-coefficient regulator and witness policies distinct, including the fact that the nominal u=0 row is not a demonstrated zero-control solution from perturbed B04 initial data.

A small independently specified nonlinear test plant demonstrates replay variation for tied linear witnesses and detects deliberately wrong control timing; B04 replay reproduction remains gated by canonical histories/conventions.
test_ids: T-REPLAY01: tied linear witnesses with distinct nonlinear replay

tickets.title: Present B04 historical tables alongside restoration diagnostics
tickets.scope: Goal: add provenance-labelled B04 reported table rows and restoration status to final comparison exports. Requirements EXP-02/03/04 and T-B04. Sources: b04-tables.md, baselines.md, b04-restoration.md, archive-selected-sources.json and b04-historical.json. Inputs are checked source transcriptions and measured artifacts when available; outputs separate historical reported values, evaluations at printed coordinates and independently reproduced results. Canonical model/control recovery is a separate module/ticket, not work to be guessed by this exporter.
acceptance: Historical B04 loading/export reports non-executable restoration diagnostics for missing canonical control bounds, first-action convention and displayed-model/terminal-result inconsistency; provisional [-1,1] belongs only to a separately identified exploratory scenario.

Preserve Table 2 policy labels and all reported terminal/objective rows with source/hash/precision metadata; recomputed printed-coordinate costs use separate columns and rounding-aware interpretation.
Display the checked stock-invariant contradiction and unrestricted-plane lower bound as restoration evidence, never as a recovered constrained optimum or solver performance target.

The reported 30.899 and 0.4 seconds are historical data, not exact unit-test or modern performance thresholds; corrected/exploratory/reproduced scenario IDs cannot overwrite the transcription identity.

A B04 export with no executable run remains useful and truthfully marks current measured fields unavailable; later reproduction columns require a canonical executable manifest and explicit source changes.

tickets.title: Benchmark module substitutions under common optimal-family outputs
tickets.scope: Goal: provide reproducible benchmark configurations auditing independent substitution axes, rather than ranking stacks with different mathematics. Requirements ALG-01/02/03/07, EXP-01/04/05 and RUN-04. Sources: modular architecture, performance-and-language.md and baselines.md. Inputs are executable analytic/scaling cases and existing registered implementations; outputs are raw runs and detailed final tables. Compare the two synthesis strategies first. Within a strategy change one LP/simplex variant, supported convex method (including Zoutendijk when separately implemented), exact set representation or equivalent conversion route at a time. New numerical adapters are prerequisites, not implemented here.
acceptance: Run both agreed strategies on T-S01/02/03 with the same problem/objective/optimal-family scope, tolerances and witness request; independent verification checks analytic optimum, admissibility and family semantics rather than identical witness coordinates.

Keep strategy, LP/simplex variant, convex optimization method, set representation, operator/converter and selector as independent configuration fields. Record selected and rejected combinations with assumptions, including basis-diagnostic requirements and convex method differentiability/reformulation support.

Where two compatible adapters exist, demonstrate replacement without changing model/objective/frontend contracts; unavailable implementations are explicitly pending and produce no invented timing rows.

Sweep dimension/horizon/constraints/representation size with fixed seeds and saved raw repetitions; distinguish cold/warm runs, end-to-end latency and submodule work, and record resource/failure limits.

Compare original objective, residuals, completeness/inclusion evidence, output sizes and time/memory together; B04 canonical reproduction activates only after restoration and historical one-witness timings retain different output-scope labels.

tickets.title: Add later exact-versus-approximate reachability comparison artifacts
tickets.scope: Goal: extend the completed two-strategy comparison protocol with separately implemented compatible inner/outer approximation methods. Requirements ALG-03/04/06, EXP-01/04/05 and RUN-04. Sources: set-representations-and-ellipsoidal-toolbox.md, modular architecture and baseline readiness notes. Inputs are explicitly related exact/reference and approximate sets plus realizability/inclusion evidence; outputs are quality/performance records and labelled final 2D figures. No new approximation algorithm, ET integration, nonlinear reachability proof or mandatory intermediate viewer is implemented by this ticket.
acceptance: Schedule this extension after the first two optimization strategies pass their common family acceptance suite; approximation comparisons cannot replace that first comparison.

Every conversion/reduction/approximation declares exact/equivalent/inner/outer/heuristic direction, assumptions, budget and evidence. Smaller volume or finitely sampled support agreement alone cannot establish containment.

Where assumptions and evidence justify it, report outer-set objective lower bounds and realizable inner-set upper bounds; distinguish terminal reachability bounds from optimizer-family enclosure and retain controls for achievable witnesses.

Compare set quality, inclusion/support error under a stated test protocol, representation size and submodule timing; never demand exact and approximate sets have identical coordinates or call finite ellipsoidal directions an exact family.

Requested exact final 2D projections use supported query operators; enclosures and samples remain labelled, with query/export costs separated and analytically known low-dimensional inclusion cases serving as independent oracles.

tickets.title: Expand independent nonlinear replay and association tests
tickets.scope: Expand replay adapter and artifact-association tests independently of the linear optimizers. Implementation tickets already ship minimum tests. B04-specific numeric reproduction requires canonical plant/control data; analytic toy plants are available now.
acceptance: For x_next=x+u+u^2, check tied linear controls (0,1) and (0.5,0.5) produce nonlinear terminal states 2 and 1.5; use an independently computed sequence oracle.
Inject shifted controls, wrong plant/problem identity, missing hold convention and truncated history; produce named diagnostics rather than silently interpolated replay.
Round-trip replay artifacts without changing linear objective/optimality evidence; preserve nonlinear residuals, units, plant versions and integration limits separately.
Missing historical parameters leave B04 replay unavailable; no toy-plant result or selected best replay witness becomes a nonlinear global optimum.

tickets.title: Expand batch sweep isolation and provenance tests
tickets.scope: Expand independent scenario-sweep tests for job ownership, resource allocation, failures, cancellation and saved provenance. RUN-02 ships minimum tests before this expansion.
acceptance: A barrier-controlled backend detects shared mutable workspaces across jobs; compare sequential/parallel mathematical answers under declared tolerances.
One failed or cancelled job cannot corrupt sibling results; whole-batch cancellation preserves each job outcome and genuine partial evidence.
Check deterministic job/result association and ordering, scenario/settings hashes, seed and algorithm identity under deliberately reordered completion.
Nested native threads and outer jobs obey the declared common resource policy; report admission-only or unsupported enforcement and test without wall-clock deadlines.

tickets.title: Review nonlinear replay adapters and linear-result associations
tickets.scope: Review replay implementation and final-artifact associations after code and independent tests exist. Validate simulation assumptions and the boundary between linear optimality and nonlinear evaluation.
acceptance: Record reviewed commits, severity, file/line findings and reproduced timing/identity counterexamples; the implementer cannot self-sign off.
Audit plant/input identity, time/hold/integration conventions, objective and unit mappings; preserve historical non-executable limitations.
Confirm replay neither mutates primary families nor promotes sampled simulation into nonlinear/global/robust evidence.
Check replay workspaces and cost accounting remain independent adapters; linked blocking fixes need independent recheck.

tickets.title: Define objective-sense and unbounded-outcome semantics
tickets.scope: Make objective direction authoritative across shared LP, convex, synthesis, and adapter contracts. Current public LP, convex, and synthesis objectives are minimization-only; unbounded means unbounded below. Source maximization requires explicit g=-f normalization including offset before program creation. Define finite bound direction and exact normalized objective/program identity, adapter status/bound translation, and contradiction handling that preserves independent supported bounds. No maximize API or global convex maximization is implied. Caller-visible tests remain part of issue #204 and are outside this documentation/backlog change.
acceptance: Specify whether all resolved objectives are normalized to minimization or whether resolved problems carry an explicit objective sense.
Define the direction and subject of finite objective bounds for each sense.
Define unbounded precisely (unbounded below or above), including how solver adapters normalize statuses.
Apply contradiction checks only after the objective direction is authoritative; preserve independently supported bounds when sanitizing a contradictory outcome.
Add caller-visible tests for minimization and maximization, including finite lower/upper bounds, supported and unsupported evidence, and unbounded/undetermined outcomes.
Update the shared contracts and adapter documentation without weakening fail-closed behavior for ambiguous sense or unsupported evidence.

native_dependency_policy: Transitive reduction of implementation prerequisites; full dependencies remain in issue bodies and the manifest. External scientific blockers are preserved.
